reason: The primary CIF is valid and explicitly ordered: it parses and expands in R3 to full-occupancy Fe36As15 (51 atoms, Z=3) in the stated 11.58812 x 11.58812 x 6.55976 A hexagonal cell, and primitive reduction gives 17 atoms with Fe12As5 stoichiometry. Periodic contacts and complete neighbor shells show no chemistry veto (minimum Fe-Fe 2.108 A, Fe-As 2.200 A, As-As 2.453 A). Indexing is strong (the trace reports all first 20 lines indexed with M20=319), but exact atomic recovery is not established: the submitted coordinates give major intensity errors at numerous observed/calculated reflections, and the trace's own instantiated-profile normalized SSE of 0.06386 corresponds to a roughly 25.3% profile residual. An independent common-profile audit gives 23.1% for the CIF and RMSE 15.7 times the baseline noise, while a Pawley-style fit on the same indexed reflection positions reaches 3.18%. Thus the cell is credible but the atomic coordinates/topology are not near the profile lower bound. The R3 model arose from a limited lower-symmetry refinement, the alternative R3 Wyckoff topology search was interrupted, and no comparable score or convergent independent solution rejects materially different coordinate/topology realizations. Another structure-solution attempt is therefore likely to add a materially different viable candidate.
